source: What have you done, Ophelia? What was that?
Oy! I-is-- wos that-- what just-- Ophelia?
What in God's name...
Ophelia? What was that? What did you do?
What am I seeing? Ophelia...?
What is this? What's happening?
Ophelia? You're... some kind of...
No. What are you?
Oh god. It's true.
What? What just...
That was me? I did that?
Quince tricked me, again. This isn't a gift. This is something horrifying.
I shouldn't use this. I should just reset this world and leave. I can't stay here.
I'm... I'm not a killer. I'm not like him.
This is evil, this power.
It doesn't matter if they'll return in the next world. This is wrong.
It's almost like a little game. Watch them run, seek them out--
No. What am I saying?
Why do I continue this? I could stop. I ought to stop. I could reset this world.
It's so easy. They don't even feel real.
I know it's not too late to turn back. To reset. To leave. But I've wrought so much.
This is sort of fun, in a sick way, isn't it? A way to play with them.
Besides, I can revive them any time I like. They won't remember a thing.
They all looked down on me. I was just some nothing girl to them.
Perhaps now I desire their fear. Crave it.
Or -- perhaps this is merely a tool I can use to amuse myself.
Either way, I clearly have no desire to give it up.
What's done cannot be undone.
I think something must have gone a bit broken in my head. Hee, hee...
Every time I kill one, I feel the strangest sense of satisfaction.
Yes, if they're all dead, I can tell something marvelous will happen!
I'll truly have won then!
What an ugly way to die.
Too simple.
Yes. Die.
That strange incident you witnessed? That was my doing. You ought to be afraid of me.
What? You?
There's a strangeness to your countenance I've never seen before.
I don't know what you are -- spirit or demon or otherwise. But no justice could apply to you.
Father, I'm the one behind that strange death.
No, nono. You must be mistaken. I must be mistaken.
I refuse to believe it. My... my sweet Ophelia...
At a time like this, I find that sort of joking absolutely inappropriate, Ophelia.
Can you not see how terrified the others are? And so ought you to be.
Not another word of that. Not until this horror is contained.
Ophelia... everything we've been through... does it mean nothing?
Please! Don't hurt anyone else!
I can kill someone without laying a hand on them. I could kill you, were I so inclined.
You've gone mad.
I've been mad a long time. This is a new gift.
Hamlet, I'm the killer. It was my doing.
I-I know. I know.
But... you wouldn't hurt me, would you, Ophelia?
Please... you are better than this. You can stop. Don't make me...
What? That strange whatever-it-was... that was you?
That's not possible. No human could have done something like that. You heard so yourself.
And I'm not human.
There are so many things you don't know about me, Hamlet. Not in this world. Not now.
I have the power to kill with a single word. I could kill you, were I so inclined.
Your... your eyes. They're...
Laertes, I'm the killer. It was my doing.
You ought to be afraid of me. I can kill someone with the merest word.
This isn't funny. Not right now. Not at a time like this.
Look at me. Look closely. You know me. Do I seem as though I'm being facetious?
The body was in a state no human could have created. That was the proclamation, wasn't it?
Surely you're not claiming... you're not human?
I was, once. But no longer.
There are things you don't know about me, Laertes. I've already killed, and I'm ready to kill again.
Why did you give me this? Why did you do this to me?
Do I detect a tinge of whinging in your voice?
I didn't ask for this 'gift' of yours.
Look at you! So petulant! Adorable.
Tell me, Ophelia. If I leave a pretty cake on your threshold, and you gorge yourself on it...
Who, pray, is to blame?
You couldn't resist. And now you've indulged. What comes next?
Still not thrilled, are we?
I'll tell you what I told you last time. Your lack of self-control is hardly my doing.
How many times shall we go round and round?
Perhaps I wanted you to understand my view of it all.
How even the most heart-wrenching human emotions become trite and silly with enough repetition.
I've been at this game for centuries. You think me a monster, I'm certain.
But someday, you'll be just like me, too. And then -- you'll know.
Oh, dear heart. We've discussed this so many times. You can stop whenever you like.
Or -- well -- how many times have you used that gift now? Been quite a few, hasn't it?
Perhaps you're just like a broken clock at this point, stuck ticking the same hour.
You've taken quite a shining to this, haven't you?
Yes. My star pupil!
Don't forget. If you kill them all by midnight on Friday evening, you'll win a special prize.
And you do seem to like prizes, don't you?
Die, then -- whoever you are.
That strange incident you heard about? That was my doing. You ought to be afraid of me.
That was-- you?
How could you pull that off? No human could have killed someone that way!
Y-you should fear what will come when your work is done.
There is no reward for the devil's agents. O-only hellfire.
What can you mean?
Are you telling me you are the one responsible for that-- that-- mauling?
It was you. You killed Gerta.
How can such a thing be possible?
I have a power no one else has. I can kill you with just two words.
It's-- the Devil's work. It must be!
The girl's possessed, made into His pawn...
S-stay away from me!
Guh-- Get away from me! From all of us!
Wah! Really?! Then you're going to kill me too, aren't you!
But, really, is that possible? After all, you're so short.
You probably can't reach Irma's cheese stash on top of the hearth, let alone my neck.
I don't need to reach you. I can kill you with a single word. I have a power--
Oh! I read this book, too!
This is the one where the main character goes to that Nunnery for Witches and learns magic, right?
And then she falls in love with her super cute canoness. Such a great series.
This isn't a story, Guilda. It's the truth.
Oh, really? You mean the cute canoness is walking around the real world somewhere? So there's hope!
Anyway, have fun playing make-believe!
S-stay away from me! I don't want to play this game anymore, Ophelia.
Tell everyone to come back out. Tell them to stop pretending.
No one is pretending, Guilda. They're all really dead.
No. No! God, this can't be real, can it?
I've had enough. First King Hamlet, now you? Spirits, demons, whoever you are: this place is a haunt.
Leave us alone. Leave us in peace. Please.
I wanted to speak to you about... us. Perhaps it's not too late to make amends.
...I cannot, Ophelia.
On board the ship, Lady Guildenstern took me aside.
I cannot be a good partner to anyone, least of all you.
I've brought harm to a lot of women. I cannot undo that. But I can reconsider my path moving forward.
Especially in light of... your uncle's passing.
And not a moment too soon, at that.
Truly—though—nothing would bring me greater joy.
After the news is made public, we should... go somewhere private. My chambers, perhaps.
I'm not that eager.
You have my word. I mean only to talk. Nothing more.
I'll find you when I can.
You wish to speak with me? Truly?
...Then let's find somewhere away from prying eyes. The riverbank, perhaps.
You always were rather fond of those kinds of places, weren't you?
You're afraid you won't make for a great King?
One of my many fears, yes. If only my father were here to guide me.
Or someone else who could offer me their thoughts...
Hamlet seeks advice on how to be a great ruler. Can you help?
Ah. I suspected this day would come, but... so soon.
There would have been a time when Hamlet and I were equals in our ignorance.
But my knowledge of the political sphere has grown these last ten years. Sometimes in ways I wish it hadn't.
I've learned some ugly lessons. Some unfortunate things about the workings of this world.
I'll speak to him and see what golden words I can give him.
Wah hah hah! I knew that boy would come around eventually.
As much as I despise the Prince, it would do my lady great harm to know I begrudged him my advice.
I'll speak to him. Fret not, Ophelia.
Hamlet? Seeking advice? Is he broken?
It's a little sad how worried it makes me to hear this.
It's a positive change, Horatio. He's a new man in some ways.
Well, that's a relief. I've got all the time in the world for him. I'll find him.
My son? Seeking... advice?
Has he... is... is all well? He isn't sick? Or raving mad?
Yes. All is well. He's ready to become King.
This is a mother's dream come true. I'll speak to him as soon as I'm able.
Oh, yes! We're full of wonderful advice! Such as 'always bring a spare meal.' And 'never do today what can be delayed indefinitely.'
Time to interrogate him!
Truth be told, I'm not certain.
But at the very least, we'll speak to him.
Though I must wonder if being a great ruler is what he truly desires.
Can you encourage Hamlet to be a great king? He's seeking advice from friends.
I've encouraged a number o' kings an' gilded men! Of course I can.
So Hamlet's lookin' for a kind word? I've got just the thing for him. Thanks fer findin' me!
Well, great might be an excessively lofty goal. Let's start with adequate.
Fine. An adequate king. I'll take it.
In that case, yes. I have a few choice words for him. Not that I expect him to listen.
But I'll try all the same.
Can you encourage Hamlet to be a great King? He seeks the advice of wise folk.
Why, I thought he'd never ask.
I remember when his father was his age. So young and impressionable.
Having a hardened, grizzled veteran by his side will make all this much easier!
Father, I would stretch to call you grizzled.
W-well, that's just because I'm your father. I can be quite the warhorse! You'll see.
I'll find him as soon as I'm able.
I bear some unfortunate information about Lady Guildenstern.
